reason: The hypothesis makes several specific mechanistic claims about entropy, diffusion, segregation, and oxidation behavior, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the unique interplay of high entropy, sluggish diffusion, and selective segregation in HEAs, so specific citations are required.
premises: High configurational entropy reduces diffusion kinetics
Reduced diffusion promotes selective segregation of oxide-forming elements to the surface
Surface segregation leads to a dense, adherent, slow-growing oxide film
The oxide film acts as an oxygen diffusion barrier, slowing oxidation
HEAs outperform conventional alloys with similar oxide-former content in oxidation resistance
